clock_dir_past: The Persian clock connector "و" ("and") always counts the fraction PAST
the stated hour -- unlike Arabic, which reuses the same "و" for its
past reading too, Persian has no symmetric "to" connector in ordinary
speech, so only the past direction is wired.  Citations: see
clock_fraction_15: Persian additive clock quarter: "ساعت سه و ربع" == three-and-a-quarter ==
03:15, the quarter counted PAST the named hour (not toward the next one).
Citation 1: UT Austin, Persian Online Resources, "To Tell the Time" --
"ساعت یک و ربع است" (sa'at yek-o rob' ast) == "It is one-fifteen."
Citation 2: talkpal.ai, "Telling Time in Persian Language" -- "3:15 -
ساعت سه و ربع (sa'at-e seh va rob')".
clock_fraction_30: Persian additive clock half: "ساعت دو و نیم" == two-and-a-half == 02:30,
the half counted PAST the named hour.
Citation 1: UT Austin, Persian Online Resources, "To Tell the Time" --
"ساعت دو و نیم است" (sa'at do-vo nim ast) == "It is two-thirty."
Citation 2: talkpal.ai, "Telling Time in Persian Language" -- "4:30 -
ساعت چهار و نیم (sa'at-e chahar va nim)".
clock_meridiem_night: The night is a band that crosses midnight, not an am marker: Wiktionary
"شب" (Persian) gives the senses "night" and "evening", so "ساعت هشت شب" is
20:00 and "ساعت سه شب" is 03:00.  The band-split lives in the resolver.

Each word is shown opening a clock time on the page named in brackets,

marker_from: Persian range "from" lead -- opens the bounded interval "از ... تا ...".
"از": Dehkhoda Dictionary and Sokhan Comprehensive Dictionary, s.v. "از"
(حرف اضافه) -- مبدأ و نقطهٔ آغاز در زمان و مکان; correlative of "تا" for the
term, as in "از ۵ ژوئن تا ۱۲ ژوئن". It is also the "since" marker
(marker_since), which is the open reading of the same starting point.
